soil-fert-039.q: Why do nutrients in vermicompost wash away less readily?
soil-fert-039.a: The worm mucus coating the castings slows nutrient release and keeps nutrients from washing away.

soil-fert-084.q: Why does rain soon after spreading urea reduce nitrogen loss?
soil-fert-084.a: It moves urea into the soil, where the ammonia it forms can react with water to become ammonium instead of escaping.

soil-fert-032.q: What is the trade-off of cold composting in a small home heap?
soil-fert-032.a: It needs no turning, but it can take up to a year and parts may go anaerobic.

soil-fert-088.q: Why might a new hügelkultur bed be less fertile at first?
soil-fert-088.a: Wood has one of the highest carbon-to-nitrogen ratios, so its decay may tie up soil nitrogen for perhaps one to two years.

soil-fert-069.q: How does a living mulch differ from a cover crop?
soil-fert-069.a: A living mulch keeps growing with the crop, whereas a cover crop is worked into the soil or killed.

soil-fert-087.q: Why can soils farmed by slash-and-char keep cropping when slash-and-burn soils are abandoned?
soil-fert-087.a: Slash-and-char keeps much of the organic carbon as stable char, and such biochar-enriched soils can sustain cropping indefinitely, while slash-and-burn soils soon lose their nutrients.

soil-fert-204.q: How does Azolla fertilize a rice paddy?
soil-fert-204.a: Its partner cyanobacterium fixes atmospheric nitrogen, which Azolla releases to the rice as it dies.

soil-fert-091.q: Why does lime have to neutralize more than the acid in the soil water?
soil-fert-091.a: Acid-forming ions held on soil colloids will otherwise restore the original pH.

soil-fert-027.q: What goes wrong if green manure is worked in too short a time before planting?
soil-fert-027.a: Nitrogen immobilization can leave too little nitrogen for the next crop.

soil-fert-060.q: Why must agricultural lime be finely ground?
soil-fert-060.a: Soil acids are weak, so only fine particles react well: those finer than 60 mesh are fully effective, while those over 8 mesh are of little value.

soil-fert-037.q: Why does adding urine help a humanure compost heap?
soil-fert-037.a: It raises the heap's temperature, helping destroy pathogens and seeds.

soil-fert-044.q: Which part of human excreta carries most of its nitrogen?
soil-fert-044.a: Urine, which can hold up to 90% of the nitrogen in human excreta.

soil-fert-202.q: What is the main advantage of coated urea?
soil-fert-202.a: It releases urea gradually, lowering the risk of fertilizer burn and allowing less frequent applications.

soil-fert-017.q: Why does fluoride from phosphate fertilizers concern livestock more than crops?
soil-fert-017.a: Plants take up little fluoride, so the risk lies with livestock that eat contaminated soil.

soil-fert-046.q: Name an alternative to mined phosphate ore.
soil-fert-046.a: Phosphorus recovered from excreta, for example as struvite from urine.

soil-water-019.q: What are the two reasons rain can fail to soak in and become surface runoff?
soil-water-019.a: The soil is already saturated, or rain arrives faster than the soil can absorb it.

soil-water-089.q: Why does the US EPA prefer silt fences to straw bales for construction sediment control?
soil-water-089.a: Straw bales often protect water quality poorly and need much upkeep.

soil-water-020.q: How does infiltration-excess overland flow differ from saturation-excess flow?
soil-water-020.a: Saturation-excess flow begins only once the soil itself is saturated, while infiltration-excess flow can start on unsaturated soil.

soil-water-023.q: Why can paving a town both worsen droughts and cause floods?
soil-water-023.a: Less water reaches groundwater, so the water table falls, while more water left on the surface causes flooding.

soil-water-085.q: Why can felling a tree on clay soil damage a nearby building?
soil-water-085.a: The soil the tree had dried heaves as the deficit reverses, rising and spreading for years, and shallow foundations move with it.

soil-water-088.q: What does a low curve number say about an area?
soil-water-088.a: Its soil is more permeable and its runoff potential low.

soil-water-050.q: How do many erosion controls work physically?
soil-water-050.a: They are barriers of vegetation or rock that absorb some of the energy of the wind or water.

soil-water-045.q: Why does long cultivation make a soil more erodible?
soil-water-045.a: It depletes organic matter, which coagulates colloids into a stronger, more stable structure.
